problem: Untrusted `host` is put into an f-string and run with `shell=True`, which allows OS command injection. The previous argv-list form did not allow this.
failure: ping("8.8.8.8; id") or ping("x$(touch /tmp/pwned)") makes /bin/sh run the injected command with the caller's privileges and returns its output in stdout; afterwards /tmp/pwned exists.
fix: Go back to the argv list `subprocess.run(["ping", "-c1", "--", host], ...)` without shell=True, and validate `host` (ipaddress.ip_address or a hostname regex).

problem: The shell now splits `host` into words, expands globs and handles redirection, so a host containing spaces, `*`, `>` or `|` is no longer passed to ping as one literal argument.
failure: ping("example.com > /tmp/x") writes ping output to /tmp/x and returns ""; ping("a b") passes two args to ping, while the old code passed the single literal 'a b'.
fix: Use the argv list form with no shell.

problem: This removes the protection the list form gave (no shell interpretation) and adds no replacement: no shlex.quote, no hostname/IP validation, no `--` separator.
failure: Any value with shell metacharacters reaches /bin/sh unescaped, e.g. ping("a`id`") runs `id`.
fix: Use the argv list `["ping", "-c1", "--", host]` and validate host.

problem: A host starting with `-` is read by ping as an option. The shell form makes this worse because one value can now carry several options.
failure: ping("-f -s 65000 victim") passes the flood and packet-size options to ping as separate options; under the old list form this was one malformed argument.
fix: Add a `--` separator in the argv list and reject hosts that start with '-'.

problem: With `shell=True`, the timeout only kills `/bin/sh`. Background or chained commands started by the shell keep running after the timeout.
failure: ping("x & sleep 1000 &") leaves an orphaned `sleep 1000` process running after the call returns or times out.
fix: Remove shell=True so the timeout kills ping directly.
